# Load libraries and data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

splist <- read.csv("data/Arctic_species_list_from_Darnis2022.csv", header = TRUE)


# The trait database
traits.lvl1 <- read.csv("../Zooplankton_trait_database/data_input/Trait_dataset_level1/trait_dataset_level1-2023-08-15.csv")
# Note that there are more trait data in excluded
# Also there are curations that are in "data/traits_level1_curated_20231027.RData")


# Taxonomy table
taxonomy <- read.csv("../Zooplankton_trait_database/data_input/taxonomy_table_20230628.csv") %>% 
  distinct(taxonID, .keep_all = TRUE)
```


# Match which taxa in the Arctic list are in the trait database
```{r}
splist.match <- splist %>% 
  select(Group, Taxonomic.Level, Scientific.Name) %>% 
  mutate(id = row_number()) %>% 
  mutate(Scientific.Name = str_trim(Scientific.Name)) %>% 
  left_join(select(taxonomy,
                   scientificName, taxonID),
            by = c("Scientific.Name" = "scientificName"))

splist.nomatch.1 <- splist.match %>% 
  filter(is.na(taxonID)) %>% 
  select(-taxonID) %>% 
  left_join(select(taxonomy,
                   verbatimScientificName, taxonID),
            by = c("Scientific.Name" = "verbatimScientificName"))

splist.nomatch.2 <- splist.nomatch.1 %>% 
  filter(is.na(taxonID)) %>% 
  select(-taxonID) %>% 
  # Move to genus level
  mutate(Genus.Name = str_extract(Scientific.Name, "[A-za-z]+")) %>% 
  left_join(select(taxonomy,
                   scientificName, taxonID),
            by = c("Genus.Name" = "scientificName")) %>% 
  mutate(Taxonomic.Level = "Genus")

# The final taxonomy matching
splist.match <- splist.match %>% 
  filter(!is.na(taxonID)) %>% 
  bind_rows(splist.nomatch.1 %>% 
              filter(!is.na(taxonID))) %>% 
  bind_rows(splist.nomatch.2) %>% 
  arrange(id) %>% 
  mutate(Group.Name = if_else(Taxonomic.Level != "Species",
                              Scientific.Name, Genus.Name)) %>% 
  mutate(Group.Name = if_else(!is.na(Genus.Name),
                              Genus.Name, Group.Name)) %>% 
  mutate(Group.Name = if_else(!is.na(taxonID),
                              Group.Name, NA)) %>% 
  select(-c(id, Genus.Name))


rm(splist, splist.nomatch.1, splist.nomatch.2)
```

# Extract whatever trait database information
```{r}
traits.arctic <- traits.lvl1 %>% 
  filter(taxonID %in% splist.match$taxonID)

traits.arctic.sum <- traits.arctic %>% 
  group_by(traitName, majorgroup, scientificName, taxonID) %>% 
  summarise(nrecords = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  group_by(traitName) %>% 
  mutate(ntaxa_trait = n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  group_by(scientificName) %>% 
  mutate(ntrait_taxa = n()) %>% 
  ungroup()

sum.by.trait <- traits.arctic.sum %>% 
  distinct(traitName, ntaxa_trait) %>% 
  arrange(-ntaxa_trait)

sum.by.taxa <- traits.arctic.sum %>% 
  distinct(scientificName, ntrait_taxa) %>% 
  arrange(-ntrait_taxa)
```

# TODO Trait 
Plot the trait distribution of the taxa found in the arctic (only species level) relative to the global trait distribution. Also do this for the allometric size distribution of Arctic copepods
```{r}
arctic.species <- splist.match %>% 
  filter(Taxonomic.Level == "Species")

traits.sub <- traits.lvl1 %>% 
  # Select a few sample traits
  # filter(traitName %in% c("carbonPDW", "bodyLength","lipidPDW")) %>% 
  filter(valueType == "numeric") %>% 
  mutate(is.arctic = if_else(taxonID %in% arctic.species$taxonID &
                               taxonRank %in% c("Species", "Subspecies"),
                             TRUE, FALSE)) %>% 
  mutate(traitValue = as.numeric(traitValue))

# Simple ggplot 
ggplot(traits.sub %>% 
         filter(traitName == "carbonPDW"), aes(traitValue, 0)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = is.arctic)) +
  # scale_x_continuous(trans = "log10") +
  theme_bw() 

# Simple boxplots
ggplot(traits.sub %>% 
         filter(traitName == "dryWeightPWW")) +
         # filter(traitName == "excretionRateN_WSDW_15C")) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = is.arctic, y = traitValue)) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "log10") +
  theme_bw()

# For numeric traits compare distribution of trait values, note that many of these might need transformation for significance testings
num.traits <- traits.lvl1 %>% 
  filter(valueType == "numeric") %>% 
  mutate(traitValue = as.numeric(traitValue)) %>% 
  # select traits with most data
  group_by(traitName) %>% 
  mutate(nrecords = n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(nrecords > 50) %>% 
  # assign if arctic (only species level)
  filter(taxonRank %in% c("Species","Subspecies")) %>% 
  mutate(is.arctic = if_else(taxonID %in% arctic.species$taxonID &
                               taxonRank %in% c("Species", "Subspecies"),
                             TRUE, FALSE)) %>% 
  # If working on species means
  group_by(traitName, is.arctic, scientificName) %>%
  summarise(traitValue = mean(traitValue),
            .groups = "drop")

# TODO Note that this could be adjusted to working with the species means... or weight the averaging based on the reciprocal of the number of records for each species.

# Calculate central tendencies
num.sum <- num.traits %>% 
  group_by(traitName, is.arctic) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            mean = mean(traitValue),
            median = median(traitValue),
            sd = sd(traitValue),
            min = min(traitValue),
            max = max(traitValue), 
            .groups = "drop")


# Get P values of Mann-Whitney test
num.wilcox <- num.traits %>% 
  # filter(traitName %in% c("carbonPDW", "bodyLength","lipidPDW")) %>% 
  group_by(traitName) %>% 
  do(w = wilcox.test(traitValue~is.arctic, data=., paired=FALSE)) %>% 
  summarise(traitName, Wilcox = w$p.value)

# merge both and tag significance levels
num.sum.sig <- num.sum %>% 
  left_join(num.wilcox, by = "traitName") %>% 
  mutate(sig = if_else(Wilcox < 0.05,
                       0.05, NA)) %>% 
  mutate(sig = if_else(Wilcox < 0.01,
                       0.01, sig)) %>% 
  mutate(sig = if_else(Wilcox < 0.001,
                       0.001, sig)) 
```


# Extract lipids trait data
Get all the lipid content data and highlight where the Arctic species are: C. hyperboreus, C. marshallae/finmarchicus/glacialis, Metridia longa.

The current dataset seems to be insufficient. There are few records with life stage information, so this makes it unclear to which size these percentages can be applied to. For the few C5 and female records, the values seem to be realistic with maximum 75% DW.
```{r}
lipids <- traits.lvl1 %>% 
  filter(traitName %in% c("lipidPDW", "lipidPWW", "lipidPAFDW"))

length(unique(lipids$taxonID))

lipids %>% 
  group_by(traitName) %>% 
  count()

lipids.sum <- lipids %>% 
  filter(lifeStage %in% c("C5","female")) %>% 
  mutate(traitValue = as.numeric(traitValue)) %>% 
  group_by(traitName, taxonID, scientificName, lifeStage) %>% 
  summarise(traitValueMean = mean(traitValue),
            traitValueSD = sd(traitValue),
            n = n(),
            .groups = "drop")
```
